answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a vault as the anchor of the cost.
